rows: What chemical is lapis lazuli's chromophore?
S₃⁻ radical anion trapped in aluminosilicate zeolite cage — charge transfer transition, not d-d
Why is ultramarine so intensely blue?
Charge transfer transitions have extinction coefficients 10³–10⁵× higher than d-d transitions
"Beyond the sea" — named for trade route from Afghanistan via Venice, not its color
Why did Renaissance painters grade their ultramarine?
Multiple purification washes yield different purity levels; first grade = pure lazurite; subsequent grades = diluted by calcite/pyrite
What makes smalt different from cobalt blue?
Smalt = powdered cobalt glass (unstable, leaches in oil, fades). Cobalt blue = cobalt aluminate spinel (stable crystal). Same metal, different matrix.
Accidental contamination: potash used to process blood → cyanide contaminated → mixed with iron solution → Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃ precipitated blue instead of red
What is Prussian blue also used as pharmaceutically?
FDA-approved antidote for thallium poisoning and Cs-137 cesium contamination (nuclear accidents). Same compound as pigment.
How did synthetic ultramarine (1826) change art?
Price dropped ~100×: blue paint accessible to everyone. Previously only affordable by wealthy patrons for special commissions.
